rules.statement: A final decree in a partition suit does not reopen the fidei commissary succession and confers an absolute title on parties to whom separate lots are given in lieu of their shares in severalty, unless the decree itself makes reference to the fidei commissum.
rules.supporting_quote: "The learned Judge overlooks the real question in the case, namely, the fact that the partition decree was based on the fidei commissary succession set forth and adopted in the plaint in that case. The trial Judge went on to give judgment on that footing. He held that the present first defendant was entitled to the 41/48 shares he had bought from his brothers and sisters and that the 7/48 shares he had inherited, he found was subject to the fidei commissum and that the present plaintiff was entitled to that fractional share subject to claims for compensation. Neither the plaintiff nor the first defendant appear satisfied with these findings."
